test_policy.notes: Kenyon "has adopted a test-optional policy for all students applying for admission" (the page calls it temporary, created in response to COVID-19, and gives no end date). SAT or ACT scores may be self-reported on the application or emailed as a PDF to admissions@kenyon.edu; official scores are needed only if admitted and enrolling. Kenyon superscores both tests. SAT Subject, AP and IB results are not required but are considered if sent. International students from schools where English is not the primary language must still submit an English proficiency test.

requirements.notes: Common App or Coalition App, Secondary School Report with transcript, Counselor Recommendation, one Teacher Evaluation (preferably from a year-long college-preparatory course taught in junior year) and a Mid-year Report. There is no application fee (CDS 2025-26, C13: no application fee). The deadlines page lists no supplemental essay among the required documents but does not say whether the Common App or Coalition application carries a Kenyon-specific writing supplement, so that field is left blank. A portfolio, up to two additional recommendations and an interview are optional. Interviews are "recommended but not required" (a virtual interview with a student fellow); the CDS (C7) marks the interview 'Considered', so it is listed as evaluative; international applicants can also use InitialView or Vericant recorded interviews. International aid applicants may use the CSS Profile or Kenyon's own international aid application, so the CSS Profile and FAFSA fields are left blank (US citizens and permanent residents file both).

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding. Decision released mid-December. The page prints month and day only (no year); the 2026-27 cycle (fall 2027 entry) is assumed because Nov 15 is the next occurrence and the dates repeat the CDS 2025-26 closing dates. The financial aid page still shows the 2026-27 award year (CSS Profile 2026-27, 2024 tax documents), so confirm before relying on these dates. Aid forms (CSS Profile or Kenyon's international aid application) are due Nov 15 for Early Decision I per the aid page; no separate international deadline is published.

deadlines.label: Early Decision II
deadlines.notes: Binding. Decision released mid-February. Aid forms are due Jan 15 per the aid page. Year assumed as for Early Decision I.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Decision released mid-March per the deadlines page; the CDS (C16-C17) lists March 23 as the beginning notification date and May 1 as the reply date. Aid forms are due Jan 15. Kenyon has no Early Action (CDS C22). Year assumed as for Early Decision I.

english_policy.waiver_notes: International students must show English proficiency "unless your primary language of instruction in secondary school is English"; all others are required to submit an English proficiency exam. Accepted: Duolingo English Test, IELTS Academic, IELTS Indicator, TOEFL and TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition. The page gives only encouraged scores (TOEFL 100, IELTS 7.0, Duolingo 130), not hard minimums. SAT/ACT do not replace the English test.

english.notes: "Score of at least 100 is encouraged" for TOEFL and TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition; no hard minimum or subscore published. No new-scale (1-6) score is published.
"Score of at least 7.0 is encouraged" for both IELTS Academic and IELTS Indicator; no hard minimum or band minimums published.
"Score of at least 130 is encouraged"; no hard minimum published.

aid.notes: Kenyon's aid page says it will "commit to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for qualifying students"; international students can apply for need-based aid with the CSS Profile (Kenyon code 1370) or Kenyon's Online International Financial Aid Application (in the admission portal after applying; applicants living in the US or Canada must use the CSS Profile). The family contribution for admitted international students stays constant in later years, and an international student admitted without aid cannot apply for aid in the four years. No page checked states a need-blind or need-aware policy for international applicants; the need-aware label rests on Kenyon's alumni magazine (Fall 2018: the College "must, for the foreseeable future, remain need-aware"), so treat it as dated. CDS 2025-26 H6: 149 nonresident undergraduates received institutional aid, average $73,082. All first-year Early Decision and Regular Decision applicants are considered for merit scholarships of $15,000 to $35,000 a year; the CDS ticks non-need-based aid as available to nonresidents.

sat.note: No SAT code on the pages checked; scores can be self-reported or emailed as a PDF to admissions@kenyon.edu. The aid page lists CSS Profile code 1370 only.

act.note: No ACT code on the pages checked; scores can be self-reported or emailed as a PDF to admissions@kenyon.edu.

toefl.note: No TOEFL code on the pages checked; pick Kenyon College by name when sending scores.

tier_notes.computer_science: Computing is a concentration, not a major; the nearest major is Mathematics and Statistics. Small program at a liberal-arts college.
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry and Neuroscience majors in a small college with no graduate programs; judged below the general tier.
tier_notes.pre_med: Pre-health is an advising path through the science majors, not a separate program; judged below the general tier.
tier_notes.economics: Economics major in a small liberal-arts department; judged below the general tier.
tier_notes.math_physics: Mathematics and Statistics and Physics majors in small departments; judged below the general tier.
tier_notes.humanities: English and Creative Writing, History, Philosophy, Classics and modern languages; the strongest area of a liberal-arts college (home of The Kenyon Review). Same letter as the general tier.
tier_notes.arts_design: Studio Art, Art History, Music, Drama, Dance and Film majors at small scale; judged below the general tier.
tier_notes.engineering: No engineering major; only dual-degree partnerships with engineering schools.
tier_notes.business: No business major (liberal-arts college); economics and pre-professional advising only.
